answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to complete a small proof-of-work puzzle before it may post or vote, with the result bound to that identity’s public key and checked by peers. One machine can still mint many keys, but each usable identity consumes measurable compute and electricity, so a Sybil attacker must pay roughly in proportion to the influence sought; there is no free zenith of identities. Keeping the puzzle modest limits the ivory-tower barrier for ordinary users, while rate limits prevent a spiral of cheap retries from bypassing the cost.
